problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate the annual budget across 20 different public infrastructure projects to maximize the overall community benefit score. The profile for each project is as follows:
* Project A: benefit score is 0.092, implementation complexity is 0.061, allocation limits [0.037, 0.371]
* Project B: benefit score is 0.199, implementation complexity is 0.257, allocation limits [0.001, 0.580]
* Project C: benefit score is 0.147, implementation complexity is 0.034, allocation limits [0.066, 0.802]
* Project D: benefit score is 0.069, implementation complexity is 0.252, allocation limits [0.042, 0.352]
* Project E: benefit score is 0.030, implementation complexity is 0.045, allocation limits [0.067, 0.858]
* Project F: benefit score is 0.123, implementation complexity is 0.139, allocation limits [0.006, 0.353]
* Project G: benefit score is 0.025, implementation complexity is 0.216, allocation limits [0.019, 0.851]
* Project H: benefit score is 0.149, implementation complexity is 0.101, allocation limits [0.076, 0.410]
* Project I: benefit score is 0.105, implementation complexity is 0.259, allocation limits [0.015, 0.352]
* Project J: benefit score is 0.129, implementation complexity is 0.090, allocation limits [0.027, 0.491]
* Project K: benefit score is 0.102, implementation complexity is 0.257, allocation limits [0.017, 0.676]
* Project L: benefit score is 0.051, implementation complexity is 0.200, allocation limits [0.004, 0.312]
* Project M: benefit score is 0.155, implementation complexity is 0.224, allocation limits [0.061, 0.402]
* Project N: benefit score is 0.137, implementation complexity is 0.106, allocation limits [0.069, 0.306]
* Project O: benefit score is 0.118, implementation complexity is 0.205, allocation limits [0.041, 0.683]
* Project P: benefit score is 0.039, implementation complexity is 0.271, allocation limits [0.064, 0.576]
* Project Q: benefit score is 0.087, implementation complexity is 0.270, allocation limits [0.084, 0.826]
* Project R: benefit score is 0.130, implementation complexity is 0.059, allocation limits [0.094, 0.866]
* Project S: benefit score is 0.148, implementation complexity is 0.296, allocation limits [0.031, 0.485]
* Project T: benefit score is 0.147, implementation complexity is 0.219, allocation limits [0.056, 0.709]

Each project must receive a budget share that falls within its specified allocation limits, and the sum of all budget shares must equal the total available budget. To ensure timely completion, the planner requires that the group of quick-delivery projects, represented by the subset Q = {B, C, D, E, F, G, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P, Q, S, T}, collectively receive at least 0.670 of the total budget. Additionally, the overall implementation complexity index for the portfolio must not exceed 0.181, and the total community benefit score must be no less than 0.096. Please determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total community benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
